Julianne Schultz asks what would happen if those services went dark and says sovereignty has become harder to define and control as Australians feel increasingly unsafe.

links.headline: Anthony Albanese talks a big game about sovereignty. But Australia remains in thrall to its ‘unreliable boyfriend’
links.excerpt: We rely on US tech platforms to provide the digital infrastructure of daily life. What happens when they all go dark? Sovereignty has become the buzzword of political rhetoric at precisely the moment it has become harder than ever to define, let alone control, and most Australians feel unsafe in the world . stories.title: You Can See Everything’s chaotic battle for the narrative about Elizabeth Holmes
stories.summary: A Guardian review says Nathan Fielder’s documentary You Can See Everything becomes a struggle among its subjects and filmmakers over who should be seen as hero or villain. The article presents that conflict around Elizabeth Holmes as an illuminating example of modern celebrity promotion.

stories.title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping
stories.summary: Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK, offering agents that can perform tasks such as booking travel and buying presents. The Guardian reports that users are being encouraged to delegate Christmas shopping to the service, although glitches have been reported.

stories.title: Nvidia shaken by scandal amid wider political new order for big tech

It places Nvidia’s troubles within a broader political realignment affecting the technology industry.
